label: False
claim: India's imports from China increased by 27% during the period April-August 2020.
doc: India's imports from China declined sharply in 2020. From January to February 2020, India's imports from China were as low as US$9.5 billion, reflecting a 12.4 per cent trade decline in the initial two months of COVID-19. Imports fell to a record low of USD 3.2 billion in both April and May 2020, coinciding with pandemic-induced lockdowns, before recovering to USD 4.8 billion in June and USD 5.6 billion in July—nearly back to the pre-lockdown level of USD 5.8 billion in March. For the first seven months of 2020, India's imports from China totalled USD 32.2 billion, still down 24.7% year-on-year. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that imports from China declined by 27.63% during April–August 2020.

doc: The United States and India report GDP growth and contraction differently. The U.S. GDP dropped by 9.1% during April to June 2020 on an annualised basis, while India's GDP contracted by 23.9%. When compared using the same reporting methodology, the U.S. GDP contraction during April to June 2020 was 9.1%.
speaker: S Gurumurthy
normalized_claim: Economic damage caused by the pandemic shows United States GDP (gross domestic product) falling by 33 percent compared to India's 23.9 percent drop.
perturb_type1_False: Economic damage caused by the pandemic shows United States GDP (gross domestic product) falling by about 30 percent compared to India's about 25 percent drop.
perturb_type2_False: Economic damage caused by the pandemic shows United States GDP (gross domestic product) falling by about 50 percent compared to India's about 12 percent drop.

label: False
claim: In Belfast, the digital sector employs 26 per cent of the workforce.
doc: A Tech Nation "Jobs & Skills Report 2020" analysed job vacancy advertising in the UK from June to August 2020 using Adzuna data, and a Times article based on it stated that in Belfast and Cambridge the tech sector employs 26% of the workforce. However, using BRES data, the two relevant industrial sectors—information and communication, and professional, scientific, and technical—employed an estimated 32,927 people in Belfast, representing 14% of the city's workforce. Counting only IT and engineering roles of the type advertised on Adzuna, an estimated 18,041 people are employed in such jobs in Belfast, representing 7.8% of Belfast's jobs.
speaker: The Times
normalized_claim: In Belfast, the digital sector employs 26 per cent of the workforce.
perturb_type1_False: In Belfast, the digital sector employs about 25 per cent of the workforce.
perturb_type2_False: In Belfast, the digital sector employs about 45 per cent of the workforce.

label: False
claim: Since 2002, South Africa’s police force has grown by 50%.
doc: The South African police force employed 132,310 people in 2002/03 and 192,277 in 2018/19, representing a growth of 45.3% over that period.
normalized_claim: Since 2002, South Africa’s police force has grown by 50%.
perturb_type1_False: Since 2002, South Africa’s police force has grown by about 50%.
perturb_type2_False: Since 2002, South Africa’s police force has grown by about 100%.

label: False
claim: Donald trump said "We have already built 300 miles of border wall."
doc: When Trump began campaigning for president, the southwest border had 654 miles of primary barriers. Under Trump, that increased by three miles to 657 miles. The Trump administration mainly replaced barriers installed by previous administrations with new ones expected to be more effective. Mexico did not pay for any construction; American taxpayers covered the costs.
speaker: Donald Trump
normalized_claim: Donald trump said "We have already built 300 miles of border wall."
perturb_type1_False: Donald trump said "We have already built about 300 miles of border wall."
perturb_type2_False: Donald trump said "We have already built about 600 miles of border wall."

label: False
claim: The Edo State government of Nigeria receives 600 million naira monthly as a security vote.
doc: Security votes are monthly budgetary allocations provided by Nigeria's federal government to the 36 states for financing security, disbursed at officials' discretion and not subject to legislative oversight or independent audit. Transparency International estimates these secretive cash expenditures add up to over $670 million (N241.2 billion) annually. In 2020, the Edo State government received 6.5 billion naira through security voting, equating to approximately 417 million naira per month.
speaker: Pastor Ize-Lyamu
normalized_claim: The Edo State government of Nigeria receives 600,000,000 naira monthly as a security vote.
perturb_type1_False: The Edo State government of Nigeria receives about 600,000,000 naira monthly as a security vote.
perturb_type2_False: The Edo State government of Nigeria receives about 1,200,000,000 naira monthly as a security vote.

doc: The first night of the 2020 Republican National Convention on Monday, August 24 was broadcast on cable and television networks. According to Nielsen, which statistically estimates the number of Americans watching TV, an estimated 17 million people tuned in to watch the first night of the convention.
